And 
Counsel for Applicant :- Kunwar Bahadur Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Sudheer Kumar Rawat Hon'ble Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.

1. Heard Sri Kunwar Bahadur Singh, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Vishwanath Nishad,
learned Additional Government Advocate for the State as well as Sri Sudheer Kumar Rawat, learned counsel for opposite party no. 2.
2.

This petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioners with the prayer to quash the chargesheet dated 03.12.2021 filed in Criminal Case No. 89454 of 2023, arising out of Case Crime No. 0741 of 2019, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Sections 3/4 of D.P. Act,
Police Station Thakurganj, District Lucknow and summoning order dated 19.08.2023 passed by learned Special Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, CBI(AP), Lucknow as well as entire proceedings of in pursuance thereof, on the basis of compromise entered between the parties.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court vide order dated 12.02.2024 directed the parties to file compromise deed before the court below concerned and the court below was directed to verify the contents and parties of the compromise deed.

4. In compliance of the aforesaid order, the compromise deed was filed before the court below and the court concerned vide report dated 11.03.2024 has verified the contents and parties of the compromise deed and submitted his report to the extent that the parties and contents of the compromise deed are genuine and they have entered into the compromise by free-will.
The report of the concerned court below dated 11.03.2024 is on record.
5. Learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 has submitted that the parties in dispute are not interested to pursue the criminal case.

6. The Apex Court in re: Unnikrishnan alias Unnikuttan vs. State of Kerala reported in (2018) 15 Supreme Court Cases 343 has observed that even if the offence(s) in question is/are not compoundable within the scope of section 320 Cr.P.C. even then considering the facts and circumstances of the case in question the Constitutional Court may allow the parties to compound such offence(s) on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.

entities.text: Unnikrishnan alias Unnikuttan vs. State of Kerala reported in (2018) 15 Supreme Court Cases 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7. Not only the above, considering the facts and circumstances of the issue in question and other dictums of Hon'ble Apex Court in re: B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and Another; 2003 (4) SCC 675, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303; State of Rajasthan vs. Shambhu Kewat, (2014) 4 SCC 149; State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Deepak (2014) 10 SCC 285; State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Manish (2015) 8 SCC 307; J.Ramesh Kamath vs. Mohana Kurup (2016) 12 SCC 179;
State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Rajveer Singh (2016) 12 SCC 471; Parbatbhai AAhir vs. State of Gujarat (2017) 9 SCC 641, the entire proceedings of the aforesaid criminal case are hereby quashed.
